Context: The Valentine's week 25% off promo brought crowds but lost money; bean prices went up in February
Options: Stop discounts entirely; cap discounts at 15%; replace discounts with a loyalty card
Why: Margins are thin since the bean price rise; the 25% promo made us busier but we earned less
Revisit when: If bean prices come back down
Original quote: From now on no discount goes over fifteen percent. Margins are too thin since beans went up. The Valentine's twenty-five percent thing got us slammed and we actually made less money.

Decision: Start a punch card: buy 9 drinks and the 10th is free
Context: Regulars asked for a reward; the 15% discount cap rules out big promos
Options: Punch card; app-based rewards; no program
Why: Rewards regulars without a store-wide discount and works out to about 10% off; no app for staff to learn
Original quote: Let's just do punch cards. Buy nine, tenth one's free. It's like ten percent, so it's under the cap, and nobody has to learn an app.

Decision: No cash refunds; store credit only
Context: The cash drawer came up short twice in February after refunds
Why: Cash refunds made the drawer impossible to reconcile
Original quote: No more cash refunds, period. Store credit only. The drawer was short twice last month and I couldn't figure out where it went.

Decision: Close at 3 pm on Mondays instead of 6 pm
Options: Keep 6 pm; close at 3 pm; close all day Monday
Why: Fewer than 10 customers come in after 3 pm on Mondays; saves about $180 a week in wages
Revisit when: In summer if foot traffic picks up
Original quote: Mondays we close at three. I counted and it's less than ten people after three o'clock. That's like a hundred eighty bucks a week in wages for nothing. We can look again in the summer.

Decision: Post on Instagram three times a week and stop paying for ads
Context: A $50 boosted post brought in about 2 visits; latte-art posts got more followers for free
Options: Keep boosting posts; organic posts only; hire someone to run social
Why: Free posts beat paid ones for us
Cost: About 2 hours a week of someone's time
Original quote: Okay, no more paid ads. Fifty bucks for two people walking in, no. The latte art posts do way better and they're free. Three posts a week, we'll see how it goes in three months.

Decision: Stay with Cascade Roasters as our bean supplier
Context: A cheaper online supplier sent a quote
Options: Stay with Cascade; switch to the online supplier
Why: Cascade is local and delivers twice a week; customers mention it by name
Revisit when: When the contract renews in January
Original quote: We're staying with Cascade. Yeah the other place is like a dollar twenty cheaper a pound, but Cascade drops off twice a week and people literally ask if we still use them. Look at it again when the contract's up in January.

Decision: No new hires until revenue is over $28k a month for two months in a row
Options: Hire a part-time barista now; wait for a revenue target
Why: Payroll is already too high a share of revenue
Cost: The current team covers busy weekends
Revisit when: When revenue passes $28k for two months straight
Original quote: I'm not hiring anyone until we do twenty-eight thousand a month two months in a row. Payroll's already like a third of everything that comes in.

Decision: Oat milk at no extra charge
Context: The 75-cent oat milk upcharge was the most common complaint
Options: Keep the upcharge; lower it to 25 cents; drop it
Why: It costs us about 15 cents a drink and the complaints weren't worth it
Cost: About 15 cents per oat milk drink
Original quote: Drop the oat milk charge. It's the number one thing people complain about and it only costs us like fifteen cents a cup.

Decision: One seasonal drink at a time; swap it monthly
Context: Three specials at once last winter crowded the menu and wasted syrup
Why: Keeps the menu simple and cuts waste on syrups nobody orders
Original quote: One seasonal drink at a time. Last winter we had three going and threw out half the syrup. One a month, that's it.

Decision: Split tips by hours worked for everyone on shift
Context: Kitchen staff felt left out when tips went only to baristas
Options: Baristas only; split by hours across all staff
Why: Everyone on the shift helps make the drinks and food happen
Cost: Baristas take home a bit less
Original quote: Tips get split by hours, everybody on the shift, kitchen too. Everyone's working, everyone gets a cut.

Context: A farmers market might move to the street next door
Options: Open 8 am to 2 pm; stay closed
Original quote: I'm thinking about Sundays. Maybe eight to two. Haven't decided, I want to ask the team first.

Decision: Renew the lease for 3 years at $4100 a month
Options: One year at $4400; three years at $4100; move
Why: Saves $3600 a year and the corner location is the business
Original quote: Signing the three-year. Forty-one hundred instead of forty-four is thirty-six hundred a year, and honestly this corner is the whole business.

Decision: Buy pastries from Ruby's Bakery instead of the grocery wholesaler
Context: About 30% of wholesale pastries were thrown out
Options: Stay with the wholesaler; switch to Ruby's
Why: Ruby's delivers smaller batches every morning so we waste less and they taste better
Original quote: We're switching to Ruby's for pastries. We were tossing almost a third of the wholesale stuff. Ruby's brings a small batch every morning. Costs a little more, like forty cents, but we stop throwing food away.

Decision: No laptops at the four window tables on weekends
Context: Weekend seating is full and some people stay three hours on one coffee
Options: Time limit on all tables; no laptops at window tables; leave it
Why: Frees the best seats for weekend customers without banning laptops everywhere
Original quote: Weekends, no laptops at the window tables. Just those four. People are camping three hours on one drip coffee while folks wait for a seat.

Context: Cascade raised bean prices again in September
Why: Drip is our best seller and cheapest drink so a quarter there covers most of the increase
Original quote: Drip goes to three twenty-five. It's what we sell most of, so a quarter on drip covers most of the bean thing without touching everything else.

Decision: Staff can comp a drink or pastry up to $10 without asking
Context: Staff kept texting the owner to approve small make-goods for unhappy customers
Options: Owner approves everything; staff can comp up to $10; up to $20
Why: Fixes small problems on the spot and stops the texts
Cost: A few extra comps a week
Original quote: "Anything under ten bucks, just comp it. Don't text me. A free latte is cheaper than a one-star review."

Decision: Shift leads can approve shift swaps without asking the owner
Context: Shift swap requests were piling up in the owner's texts
Options: Owner approves all swaps; shift leads approve swaps
Why: Shift leads are on site and know who can cover
Original quote: "Shift leads can okay swaps. As long as the shift's covered, I don't need to know."
